title: How to Write the Perfect LifeInvader Car Ad in GTA RP
excerpt: A clean, well-formatted LifeInvader car ad sells faster and looks more professional in-character. Here's the format experienced Grand RP and Eclipse RP players actually use.
author: My Roleplay

content.text: If you've spent any time on a GTA RP server like Grand RP or Eclipse RP, you already know the LifeInvader marketplace lives and dies on how well an ad is written. A sloppy, run-on ad gets scrolled past. A clean one gets replies in seconds.
Start with the transaction type

Every good car ad opens with whether you're selling, buying, or trading. This single word tells the reader everything they need before they even see the car's name — don't bury it in the middle of the sentence.
Name the car exactly
Use the car's actual in-game name, not a nickname. "Selling a Zentorno" reads better and gets found in search/chat filters faster than "selling my fast supercar."
List configuration and extras clearly

Buyers care about whether the car is fully or partially configured, and whether it comes with visual upgrades, insurance, tuning parts, a turbo kit, or a drift kit. List these as a short, comma-separated group rather than scattering them across multiple lines.

items: Full or partial configuration
Visual upgrades
Insurance included or not
Tuning parts, turbo kit, or drift kit

content.text: End with a clear price
Close with a price or budget. If you're open to offers, say "negotiable" rather than leaving it blank — an ad with no price gets fewer serious replies.

title: LifeInvader House Ads: Complete Formatting Guide for Grand RP
excerpt: House and apartment ads have more moving parts than car ads — garage space, warehouse space, features, and view. Here's how to lay them out so buyers actually understand what they're getting.
author: My Roleplay

content.text: House and apartment ads on LifeInvader tend to be the longest and most detail-heavy ads in the marketplace, because buyers are comparing multiple properties at once. The more scannable your ad is, the more likely it survives that comparison.
Lead with what it is
State immediately whether it's a house or an apartment, and its number if it has one. This is the first filter buyers apply.
Group garage and warehouse space together
Storage space is one of the biggest value drivers for a property in GTA RP. List garage slots (2, 5, 9, or 25 g.s.) and warehouse slots (3, 4, or 5 w.h.) as their own clearly labeled group.
Call out standout features

A garden, custom interior, helipad, tennis court, long driveway, or swimming pool are all things buyers specifically search for. Don't let them get lost in a wall of text — a short list works better than a paragraph.

items: Garden
Custom interior
Helipad
Tennis court
Long driveway
Swimming pool

content.text: Mention the view and location last

View quality and location (Vinewood Hills, Rockford Hills, Paleto Bay, and so on) matter, but they're secondary to space and features for most buyers — save them for the end of the ad, right before the price.

title: Business Ads on LifeInvader: A Beginner's Guide for GTA RP Entrepreneurs
excerpt: Buying or selling a business on LifeInvader works differently from cars and houses — especially plantations. Here's what new GTA RP players get wrong.
author: My Roleplay

content.text: Business ads are where a lot of newer GTA RP players trip up, mostly because business types on most servers aren't uniform — some are numbered locations, some are plantations with bed-count tiers, and some are just generic storefronts.
Plantations are a special case

If you're advertising a plantation, always include its bed-count category — 10-Bed, 15-Bed, or 20-Bed. This single detail changes the expected price range dramatically, and omitting it is the single most common mistake in plantation ads.
Include the business number when the location isn't unique
Businesses like 24/7 stores, barber shops, or car markets often exist in multiple locations across the map. Always include the business number so buyers know exactly which one you mean.
Location still matters
Even with a business number, naming the general area — Vespucci Canals, Sandy Shores, Richman — helps buyers who are scanning quickly and mentally filtering by neighborhood.

As with car and house ads, close with a clear price or "negotiable." Business ads without a price get significantly fewer serious offers, since buyers are usually comparing several listings before committing to one.

title: Clothing & Item Ads on LifeInvader Explained
excerpt: Clothing and item ads look simple but have small formatting details — color, gender, trading, and bulk pricing — that make a real difference in how fast they sell.
author: My Roleplay

content.text: Clothing and item ads are usually the shortest ads on LifeInvader, but that also means small mistakes stand out more. Here's what separates a quick sale from an ad nobody replies to.
Clothing ads: color and gender first
Lead with the color and, if relevant, whether the piece is for men or women, before the item name. "Selling red Alaska winter jacket for men" scans faster than putting those details at the end.
Trading option changes the whole sentence
If you're open to trading rather than a straight sale, say so explicitly — "selling or trading" — rather than only mentioning it in a follow-up reply. It saves everyone time.
Item ads: up to three items, priced clearly

When bundling multiple items in one ad (most servers cap this around three), decide up front whether you're pricing them together as one total or individually. If pricing individually, use "respectively" after listing all prices in the same order as the items, so there's no ambiguity about which price belongs to which item.
In bulk changes buyer expectations

Marking an item ad as "in bulk" signals you have a large, repeatable quantity available — useful for players building a stock, not just a one-off buyer. Don't use it if you only have a handful of the item.

title: 10 GTA RP Server Rules Every Newcomer Should Know
excerpt: Before you ever post a LifeInvader ad, make sure you understand the baseline rules most GTA RP servers enforce — breaking these gets people banned in their first week.
author: My Roleplay

content.text: Every GTA RP server has its own detailed rulebook, but almost all of them share a common core. If you're new, learning these first will save you from an early ban and a bad first impression.

items: No random death match (RDM) — you need in-character justification before engaging in violence.
No fail RP — actions must make sense for your character and the situation.
No metagaming — don't use out-of-character information (Discord, streams) in-character.
No powergaming — don't force actions on other players they can't reasonably escape or refuse.
Combat logging is bannable — don't disconnect to avoid an in-progress scene.
Vehicle deathmatch (VDM) is treated the same as RDM on most servers.
New Life Rule — your character generally forgets the events leading to their death.
Stay in character in IC voice/text channels — OOC chatter belongs in designated channels.
Advertise fairly — LifeInvader ads should reflect real in-game listings, not scams.
Read your specific server's full rules — this list is the common baseline, not a replacement.
